name: Companion
description: Your Companion on your glasses: a warm, private personal assistant that remembers. Ask a question and get a spoken answer grounded in your own Companion Memory; say "remember this" to save something forever; ask what you told it weeks ago and it will recall. Memory is opt-in — until you turn on "Remember our conversations" nothing is recalled or stored, and what is stored lives on your own Companion appliance, never a third-party cloud. REQUIRED PERMISSIONS (grant these in the MentraOS Developer Console at console.mentra.glass — the app_config.json schema has no permissions field): MICROPHONE (required — the voice loop cannot work without it); CAMERA (optional — only for the "take a photo" tool, which is off by default); CALENDAR (optional — only for the "what's on my calendar" tool); NOTIFICATIONS and LOCATION (optional — reserved for future context features). Every optional capability degrades gracefully: if the permission is not granted or the hardware is absent, the core voice loop keeps working.

tools.description: Save something to the wearer's long-term Companion Memory so it can be recalled later. Use for facts, preferences, names, codes, reminders and anything the wearer explicitly wants kept.

content.description: The exact fact or note to remember, phrased so it will still make sense months from now.

tools.description: Search the wearer's long-term Companion Memory and return what is relevant to a question. Use when the wearer asks what they said, what they know, or anything about their own past.

query.description: What to search the wearer's memory for, in natural language.

tools.description: Tell the wearer what is coming up next on their calendar, using the calendar events MentraOS has synced to this session. Requires the CALENDAR permission.
Capture a photo through the glasses camera and save a memory fragment describing it. Requires the CAMERA permission and the 'Allow take a photo' setting.

note.description: Optional note describing why the photo is being taken or what is in view.
